note: Canonical mock-test content. Read by the backend seed script (backend/scripts/seed_mock_tests.py) and imported by the frontend (frontend/lib/data/mockTests.ts). questionType must be one of app.question_types.QuestionType: mcq | numeric | essay.

papers.title: Hardcore JEE Mock Test — Paper 2
papers.description: Full-length JEE Main 2026 pattern paper: 75 questions across Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics — 20 MCQs plus 5 numerical-value questions per subject. Advanced conceptual difficulty, timed 3 hours, with detailed solutions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A photon of energy 5 eV ejects electrons from a metal of work function 2 eV. The stopping potential is:
questions.explanation: Kmax = 5 − 2 = 3 eV = eVs, hence Vs = 3 V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In a series LCR circuit at resonance, the impedance is:
questions.explanation: At resonance X_L = X_C, so the net reactance is zero and Z = R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A uniform rod of length L and mass M is hinged at one end and released from rest from the horizontal. Its angular speed when it becomes vertical is:
questions.explanation: Loss of COM potential energy MgL/2 = (1/2)Iω² with I = ML²/3, so ω² = 3g/L.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A simple pendulum has time period T at a place where g is known. If its length is increased by 44%, the percentage increase in T is approximately:
questions.explanation: T ∝ √L, so T′/T = √1.44 = 1.2 — a 20% increase.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to its velocity. If its kinetic energy is quadrupled, its radius becomes:
questions.explanation: r = p/(qB) and p ∝ √K, so r ∝ √K. Four times K gives twice r.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle of mass m moving with speed v collides elastically head-on with a stationary particle of mass 3m. The speed of the incident particle after collision is:
questions.explanation: For an elastic 1D collision, v₁′ = (m₁−m₂)/(m₁+m₂)·v = (m−3m)/(4m)·v = −v/2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A wire of resistance R is stretched uniformly to twice its original length without change of volume. Its new resistance is:
questions.explanation: Volume is constant, so the area halves: R′ = ρ(2L)/(A/2) = 4R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A satellite is moved from a circular orbit of radius R to another circular orbit of radius 4R around Earth. The ratio of its orbital speeds is:
questions.explanation: Orbital speed v = √(GM/r), so v_R / v_4R = 2, i.e. 2:1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A liquid rises to height h in a capillary of radius r. If the capillary radius is doubled and surface tension is unchanged, the new rise is:
questions.explanation: Capillary rise h = 2T cosθ/(ρ g r), hence h ∝ 1/r.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A block of mass m is on a rough horizontal surface (coefficient μ). A horizontal force F is applied. The block is just about to move when F = μmg. If the same force is instead applied at an angle θ above the horizontal, the least force required to start motion is:
questions.explanation: At limiting motion F cosθ = μ(mg − F sinθ), so F(cosθ + μ sinθ) = μmg and F = μmg/(cosθ + μ sinθ).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In Young's double-slit experiment, if both slit separation and wavelength are doubled, fringe width becomes:
questions.explanation: Fringe width β = λD/d; doubling both λ and d leaves β unchanged.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A coil of N turns and area A rotates with angular speed ω in uniform magnetic field B. The maximum induced emf is:
questions.explanation: Flux = NAB cos ωt, so the maximum induced emf is NABω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: For a p-n junction diode under forward bias, the depletion-layer width:
questions.explanation: Forward bias lowers the barrier potential and narrows the depletion region.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two charges +q and +4q are separated by distance d. The electric field is zero at a point between them. Its distance from +q is:
questions.explanation: q/x² = 4q/(d−x)². Taking positive roots, d−x = 2x, so x = d/3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: One mole of an ideal monatomic gas expands adiabatically until its volume doubles. If initial temperature is T, the final temperature is:
questions.explanation: TV^(γ−1) = constant with γ = 5/3, so T₂/T₁ = (V₁/V₂)^(2/3) = 2^(−2/3).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A small block slides from rest down a smooth track through a vertical height h and enters a rough horizontal patch of length L with coefficient μ. It stops exactly at the far end. The required height is:
questions.explanation: At the bottom the potential energy lost is mgh and the rough patch removes μmgL, so mgh = μmgL and h = μL.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle moves on the x-axis with x(t) = t³ − 6t² + 9t (SI units). The total distance travelled during 0 ≤ t ≤ 4 s is:
questions.explanation: v = 3(t−1)(t−3), so turning points are t = 1 and 3. x(0) = 0, x(1) = 4, x(3) = 0, x(4) = 4, giving a total distance of 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm forms a real image at 60 cm from the lens. The object distance is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two masses m and 2m are connected by a light string over a frictionless pulley. The tension in the string is:
questions.explanation: Acceleration a = (2m−m)g/(3m) = g/3. For m, T − mg = ma, so T = 4mg/3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A capacitor C charged to potential V is connected in parallel to an uncharged capacitor 2C. The final common potential is:
questions.explanation: Charge conservation: CV = (3C)V_f, so V_f = V/3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle executes SHM with amplitude 5 cm and angular frequency 4 rad/s. Find its maximum speed in cm/s.
questions.explanation: v_max = ωA = 4 × 5 = 20 cm/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A body is projected vertically upward with speed 30 m/s. Take g = 10 m/s². Find the maximum height in metres.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A 10 μF capacitor is charged to 100 V. Its stored energy, expressed in mJ, is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A 2 kg block moving at 6 m/s collides and sticks to a 1 kg block at rest. Find the common speed in m/s.
questions.explanation: Momentum conservation: 2 × 6 = 3v, so v = 4 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An electron is accelerated through a potential difference of 100 V. Using e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, its kinetic energy in eV is numerically:
questions.explanation: An electron gaining energy through a potential difference of 100 V gains 100 eV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which carbocation is most stabilized by hyperconjugation?
questions.explanation: More alkyl groups provide more hyperconjugative structures, so the tert-butyl carbocation is the most stabilized of these.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The conjugate base of H2PO4⁻ is:
questions.explanation: Removal of one proton from H2PO4⁻ gives HPO4²−.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The number of atoms in one face-centred cubic unit cell effectively belonging to the unit cell is:
questions.explanation: The 8 corners contribute 1 atom and the 6 faces contribute 3 atoms, for a total of 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For a reaction with rate law r = k[A]²[B], if [A] is doubled and [B] is halved, the rate changes by:
questions.explanation: Rate factor = 2² × ½ = 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: 10 g of CaCO3 (M = 100 g mol⁻¹) is heated completely. The volume of CO2 at STP is approximately:
questions.explanation: n(CaCO3) = 0.1 mol, giving 0.1 mol CO2. At STP, V = 2.24 L.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which oxide is amphoteric?
questions.explanation: Al2O3 reacts with both acids and strong bases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: At equilibrium, increasing pressure for N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g) shifts equilibrium:
questions.explanation: Pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles: 2 versus 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The oxidation state of chromium in Cr2O7²− is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which reagent converts a primary alcohol to an aldehyde without significant over-oxidation?
questions.explanation: PCC oxidizes primary alcohols selectively to aldehydes under anhydrous conditions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which complex is expected to be diamagnetic?
questions.explanation: [Fe(CN)6]4− has Fe2+, d6 with strong-field CN−, giving low-spin t2g6 with all electrons paired.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which compound gives a positive iodoform test?
questions.explanation: Ethanol is oxidized to ethanal, which contains the CH3CO− unit required for the iodoform reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The standard cell potential for a galvanic cell is positive when:
questions.explanation: ΔG° = −nFE°cell. A spontaneous standard reaction has ΔG° < 0 and E°cell > 0.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which species has the largest bond order according to molecular orbital theory?
questions.explanation: Removing an electron from an antibonding π* orbital raises the bond order: O2 = 2, O2+ = 2.5, O2− = 1.5, O2²− = 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The major product of propene with HBr in the absence of peroxide is:
questions.explanation: Electrophilic addition follows Markovnikov orientation, giving 2-bromopropane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Among BF3, NH3, H2O and CH4, the molecule with zero dipole moment is:
questions.explanation: BF3 is trigonal planar and symmetric, so the bond dipoles cancel.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Aniline is less basic than cyclohexylamine mainly because in aniline:
options: lone pair is delocalized into benzene ring
questions.explanation: The nitrogen lone pair participates in resonance with the aromatic ring, reducing its availability for protonation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A buffer contains equal concentrations of CH3COOH and CH3COONa. If Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵, the pH is closest to:
questions.explanation: Henderson-Hasselbalch: pH = pKa + log 1 = pKa = −log(1.8 × 10⁻⁵) = 4.74.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which polymer is formed by condensation polymerization?
questions.explanation: Nylon-6,6 forms from a diamine and a diacid with elimination of small molecules, so it is a condensation polymer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For an ideal solution obeying Raoult's law, the partial vapour pressure of component A is:
questions.explanation: Raoult's law: p_A = x_A P°_A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A first-order reaction has half-life 20 min. The time required for 87.5% completion is:
questions.explanation: 12.5% remains = 1/8 = (1/2)³, so three half-lives = 60 min.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: How many stereoisomers are possible for a molecule with two independent chiral centres and no meso form?
questions.explanation: For n = 2 independent centres the maximum is 2ⁿ = 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: How many moles of electrons are required to reduce 1 mol of MnO4⁻ to Mn2+ in acidic medium?
questions.explanation: Mn(+7) to Mn(+2) requires 5 electrons per Mn.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For a first-order reaction, if k = 0.0231 min⁻¹, its half-life in minutes is approximately:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: One mole of an ideal gas expands reversibly and isothermally from 10 L to 20 L at 300 K. Using R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, the work in J is approximately 1729. Find the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The pH of 0.001 M HCl at 25°C is:
questions.explanation: A strong acid fully dissociates, so [H⁺] = 10⁻³ M.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The minimum value of x + 1/x for x > 0 is:
questions.explanation: By AM-GM, x + 1/x ≥ 2, with equality at x = 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The general solution of dy/dx = 2x(1 + y) is:
questions.explanation: dy/(1 + y) = 2x dx, so ln|1 + y| = x² + C, giving 1 + y = Ce^(x²).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The distance between the parallel lines 3x + 4y − 7 = 0 and 3x + 4y + 8 = 0 is:

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The sum to infinity of 3 + 1 + 1/3 + … is:
questions.explanation: Geometric series with a = 3 and r = 1/3: S = 3/(1 − 1/3) = 9/2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: ∫₀¹ x/(1 + x²) dx equals:
questions.explanation: Let u = 1 + x², so du = 2x dx. The integral is ½ ln(1 + x²) evaluated from 0 to 1 = (1/2) ln 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: lim(x→0) [sin x − x cos x]/x³ equals:
questions.explanation: Using expansions, sin x − x cos x = (x − x³/6) − (x − x³/2) + … = x³/3 + …, so the limit is 1/3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The equation of the tangent to x² + y² = 25 at (3, 4) is:
questions.explanation: For x² + y² = a² the tangent at (x₁, y₁) is xx₁ + yy₁ = a², giving 3x + 4y = 25.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the roots of x² − 6x + k = 0 are in the ratio 1:2, then k equals:
questions.explanation: The roots are a and 2a, so 3a = 6 and a = 2. Their product is 2a² = 8, hence k = 8.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: How many 5-digit numbers can be formed from digits 0,1,2,3,4,5 without repetition and divisible by 5?
questions.explanation: The last digit must be 0 or 5. If it is 0, the other four positions give 5P4 = 120. If it is 5, the leading digit has 4 choices (1–4) and the remaining four positions give 4P4 = 24, so 96. Total 216.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If z satisfies |z − 1| = |z + 1|, then z lies on:
questions.explanation: Equidistance from (1, 0) and (−1, 0) gives x = 0, the imaginary axis.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The angle between vectors a = (1, 1, 0) and b = (1, 0, 1) is:
questions.explanation: The dot product is 1 and each magnitude is √2, so cos θ = 1/2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The area enclosed between y = x and y = x² from x = 0 to 1 is:

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: For f(x) = x³ − 3x, the local maximum value is:
questions.explanation: f′ = 3(x² − 1) gives critical points at ±1, and f″ = 6x, so x = −1 is a maximum with f(−1) = 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The coefficient of x³ in (1 + x)⁸ is:
questions.explanation: The coefficient is C(8, 3) = 56.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The shortest distance between the skew lines r = (1,0,0) + λ(1,1,0) and r = (0,1,1) + μ(1,0,1) is:
questions.explanation: Distance = |(b − a)·(d₁ × d₂)| / |d₁ × d₂|. Here b − a = (−1, 1, 1) and d₁ × d₂ = (1, −1, −1), whose magnitude is √3, with a dot product of −3. So the distance is 3/√3 = √3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A fair coin is tossed 6 times. Probability of exactly 3 heads is:

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The number of solutions of tan x = √3 in 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π is:
questions.explanation: x = π/3 + nπ, which in [0, 2π] gives x = π/3 and 4π/3 — two solutions.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The number of real roots of x⁴ − 5x² + 4 = 0 is:
questions.explanation: Let y = x²: y² − 5y + 4 = (y − 1)(y − 4), so x = ±1, ±2 — four real roots.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If A is a 2×2 matrix with det A = −2, then det(3A) equals:
questions.explanation: For a 2×2 matrix det(3A) = 3² det A = 9(−2) = −18.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The principal value of sin⁻¹(sin 5π/6) is:
questions.explanation: The principal range of sin⁻¹ is [−π/2, π/2]. Since sin(5π/6) = 1/2, the answer is π/6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The number of diagonals in a polygon is 35. Find the number of sides.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The sum of the first 20 positive integers that are divisible by 3 is:

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If ∫₀^a 2x dx = 9 for a > 0, find a.
questions.explanation: ∫₀^a 2x dx = a² = 9, hence a = 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The number of real solutions of |x − 1| + |x + 1| = 4 is:
questions.explanation: For |x| ≥ 1 the expression is 2|x| = 4, so x = ±2; for |x| < 1 it equals 2, which gives no solutions.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the determinant |1 1 1; 1 2 3; 1 3 6| equals N, find N.
